## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science at Paderborn University
## Interests
* Cybersecurity, SOC operations, and VAPT
* Python development and network systems

## Fun fact
I once spent hours debugging a network script only to realize a single misplaced router rule was simulating an entire digital traffic jam.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI coding assistants are fantastic accelerators for writing code, drafting initial test cases, and quickly parsing documentation. However, they frequently lack holistic system-level context and can quietly introduce subtle logic flaws or security vulnerabilities. Developers must remain the critical gatekeepers, actively reviewing and validating every line generated rather than blindly trusting the output.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Software engineering will shift from writing raw code line-by-line to orchestrating autonomous, multi-agent systems that handle end-to-end design, implementation, and deployment workflows. Developers will transition into high-level system architects and security auditors who define guardrails, constraints, and intent while AI agents manage iterative implementation. Cross-domain expertise; especially in security, reliability, and edge-case validation, will become even more critical as the volume of generated code scales exponentially.

## My hot take on AI
AI won't replace Human minds, rather it will provide peace of mind to humans (Caution or Note: If they know how to use it).

# Pratham



## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science (Informatik) at Paderborn University, B.Sc. in Computer Science from the University of Mumbai.



## Interests

Cybersecurity, AI, and Anime.



## Fun fact

I'm really into DIY audio and love building my own custom home theater systems in my free time.



## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is an incredible asset for generating boilerplate code and automating repetitive tasks, but it often glosses over critical security details. Developers still need a deep, hands-on understanding of network protocols and hardware interfaces to ensure the generated code is actually secure and functional.



## Where software engineering will be in 5-10 years

The role of a software engineer will likely shift from writing raw syntax to designing system architectures and auditing AI-generated logic. AI will handle the bulk of implementation, while humans will focus on complex problem-solving, hardware interoperability, and patching inevitable security blind spots.



## My hot take on AI

AI will write 90% of our code, and we will spend 100% of our time patching the security vulnerabilities it introduces.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI coding assistants are fantastic accelerators for writing code, drafting initial test cases, and quickly parsing documentation. However, they frequently lack holistic system-level context and can quietly introduce subtle logic flaws or security vulnerabilities. Developers must remain the critical gatekeepers, actively reviewing and validating every line generated rather than blindly trusting the output.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Software engineering will shift from writing raw code line-by-line to orchestrating autonomous, multi-agent systems that handle end-to-end design, implementation, and deployment workflows. Developers will transition into high-level system architects and security auditors who define guardrails, constraints, and intent while AI agents manage iterative implementation. Cross-domain expertise; especially in security, reliability, and edge-case validation, will become even more critical as the volume of generated code scales exponentially.

## My hot take on AI
AI won't replace Human minds, rather it will provide peace of mind to humans (Caution or Note: If they know how to use it).

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science at Paderborn University
## Interests
* Cybersecurity, SOC operations, and VAPT
* Python development and network systems

## Fun fact
I once spent hours debugging a network script only to realize a single misplaced router rule was simulating an entire digital traffic jam.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI coding assistants are fantastic accelerators for writing code, drafting initial test cases, and quickly parsing documentation. However, they frequently lack holistic system-level context and can quietly introduce subtle logic flaws or security vulnerabilities. Developers must remain the critical gatekeepers, actively reviewing and validating every line generated rather than blindly trusting the output.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Software engineering will shift from writing raw code line-by-line to orchestrating autonomous, multi-agent systems that handle end-to-end design, implementation, and deployment workflows.
